sections.h2: Bahrain VAT and Compliance in ERPNext
sections.intro: Bahrain introduced VAT at 5% in 2019 and raised it to 10% from 1 January 2022. ERPNext Bahrain VAT setups follow NBR rules:

items.text: Standard rate of 10%, with zero-rated and exempt supplies as separate tax templates
Tax invoices with your VAT number, the customer's VAT number where required, and Arabic text
Reverse charge on imported services, posted automatically
VAT return figures prepared box by box for filing with the NBR
Audit trail showing who created or changed every invoice

outro.html: ERPNext VAT setup Bahrain projects test every template against real invoices before go-live. Our ERPNext NBR compliance checks also cover zero-rated exports and supplies to Saudi customers. For official guidance, see the National Bureau for Revenue.

paragraphs.text: Bahrain has no general corporate income tax, but large multinational groups with global revenue of €750 million or more fall under the domestic minimum top-up tax introduced from 2025. Most local businesses are outside its scope, yet clean entity-level books, related-party tags and audit trails still matter for banks, investors and partners. An ERPNext implementation company Bahrain groups hire should set these up from the start, because adding them later means re-coding past entries.

Bahrain has not yet made e-invoicing mandatory, and the NBR has not announced a go-live date. The NBR has, however, studied a central e-invoicing platform, and it already allows businesses to issue and keep electronic invoices without prior approval. ERPNext Bahrain e-invoicing readiness means clean customer data and standard invoice fields today, so you can connect quickly once rules are published. An ERPNext implementation company Bahrain clients hire should track this for you, and we review it every quarter.

The Bahraini dinar is divided into 1,000 fils, so prices, taxes and totals need three decimal places. ERPNext BHD accounting is set to three decimals throughout, from item prices to VAT and bank reconciliation, so totals match to the fil and VAT returns agree with your books.

paragraphs.html: Many Bahrain businesses buy from or sell to Saudi Arabia every day. ERPNext handles BHD and SAR side by side, with exchange gains and losses calculated automatically, and keeps Saudi customers' VAT details for correct invoicing. Groups with companies in both countries can run them in one ERPNext system, each with its own books and tax rules. Inter-company sales across the causeway post on both sides automatically, so month-end consolidation takes hours, not days. For Saudi requirements, see ERPNext implementation in Saudi Arabia.

ERPNext's HR app handles attendance, leave, salary components and end-of-service benefits. It tracks Social Insurance Organization (SIO) contributions for each employee and produces salary payment files for your bank. Bahrainisation reports show your nationality mix by department. Work permit and CPR expiry dates trigger reminders before renewal, and staff can apply for leave and download payslips on their phones. For the full setup, see ERPNext HR and payroll for the GCC.

paragraphs.text: ERPNext for Bahrain traders focuses on landed cost and stock control. ERPNext for Bahrain contractors relies on project budgets and retention tracking. Our ERPNext solutions Bahrain clients all use the same core system, configured for their sector.

Bahrain's malls and high streets are busy, and retailers need tills that update stock and accounts instantly. ERPNext's point of sale works on a tablet or desktop, prints VAT-compliant receipts with Arabic text and keeps selling during short internet drops. Stock moves between stores and the warehouse are tracked, and loyalty points and price rules apply automatically. An ERPNext implementation company Bahrain retailers rely on should test the till with real staff before launch, and we always do.

paragraphs.html: Most Bahrain clients come from Tally, QuickBooks or spreadsheets. We move customers, suppliers, items, opening balances and open invoices, with VAT numbers checked for every record, and your old system stays live until the trial balance matches. An ERPNext implementation company Bahrain finance teams trust should finish every migration with a signed balance check. See ERPNext data migration.

items.q: Does ERPNext support Bahrain VAT at 10%?
items.a: Yes. We set up standard, zero-rated and exempt supplies, reverse charge and Arabic tax invoices, then prepare VAT return figures for filing with the NBR.

items.q: Can ERPNext prepare the figures for our NBR filing?
items.a: Yes. ERPNext produces the figures for each box of the VAT return from your invoices and bills. Your accountant reviews them and files on the NBR portal.
Yes. ERPNext can be set to three decimal places for prices, taxes and totals, so amounts match to the fil. We set this at the start, before any data is imported.
Not yet. The NBR has not announced a mandatory e-invoicing date. We prepare your data and invoice fields now, so the change is quick when rules are published.

items.q: How long does an ERPNext project take in Bahrain?
items.a: A single company usually goes live in 8–12 weeks. Groups with companies in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia take 12–14 weeks. A good ERPNext implementation company Bahrain clients hire will give these dates in writing.

items.q: What does an ERPNext project cost in Bahrain?
items.a: The price depends on users, companies, modules and stores. ERPNext itself has no licence fee. After a short discovery call, an ERPNext implementation company Bahrain businesses can trust should send a fixed quote with every line item listed, and ours does.
